title: Understanding Trap Siphonage: The S-Trap Mistake
description: When an S-trap is installed without proper venting, wastewater rushing down the vertical drop creates a self-siphoning vacuum. This vacuum pulls the standing water out of the trap dip, destroying the liquid seal that blocks dangerous sewer gases from entering the room. Modern plumbing codes require P-traps connected to a vent pipe within an allowable distance to equalize atmospheric pressure. Understanding how trap siphonage occurs helps installers avoid this common defect, ensuring safe indoor air quality and reliable fixture drainage. Always consult local code tables for maximum unvented trap arm lengths.

Understanding Trap Siphonage: The S-Trap Mistake

When an S-trap is installed without proper venting, wastewater rushing down the vertical drop creates a self-siphoning vacuum. This vacuum pulls the standing water out of the trap dip, destroying the liquid seal that blocks dangerous sewer gases from entering the room. Modern plumbing codes require P-traps connected to a vent pipe within an allowable distance to equalize atmospheric pressure. Understanding how trap siphonage occurs helps installers avoid this common defect, ensuring safe indoor air quality and reliable fixture drainage. Always consult local code tables for maximum unvented trap arm lengths.
